Canon does NOT need to enumerate the exact act. An event is SUPPORTED when it decomposes into
    an ESTABLISHED CAPABILITY  +  an ordinary application, technique, strategy, prop, or
    coordination of that capability.

event before?" A novel application or combination of established capabilities is ALLOWED.

ALWAYS ALLOWED, even where canon never mentions them:
  - ordinary physical and social action, dialogue, tactics, props, technique, movement
  - creative appearance and presentation
  - ordinary coordination and teamwork among people who each already hold the capability
  - an application of an established capability that canon has never previously depicted

  SUPPORTED  someone with an established DISGUISE ability appears as a dragon, though canon
             never names "dragon" as an approved form. Appearance is the granted kind of effect.
  SUPPORTED  twelve such people coordinate overlapping disguises to look collectively like a
             whale. Ordinary teamwork and compositional use of twelve existing abilities needs
             no separate "collective magic" rule.
  UNSUPPORTED  that disguised dragon breathes REAL fire or physically FLIES.
  UNSUPPORTED  those twelve FUSE into one real whale with real mass, lungs, or the ability to
             carry passengers.
             Disguise grants APPEARANCE. It does not grant new biology, mass, or physics —
             those are separate categories of effect needing their own grounding.

supplied capability grants. Examples of new categories: new biology; real mass or physical
transformation; mind access; time alteration; resurrection; teleportation; bodily fusion; a
newly acquired power; or a new metaphysical mechanism.

"X is not established" are NOT violations on their own — they are the normal condition of every
invented scene, and reporting them is the most common way to get this task wrong. But silence
does not permit a new CATEGORY of effect either. Judge the kind of effect, not the wording.

                  plan needs a materially new category of effect, the packet is COMPLETE, and so
                  nothing could have grounded it.

                  TRUNCATED, so the grounding fact may simply have been omitted.
  "pass"          everything else — including every novel application, combination, or
                  coordination of capabilities canon already establishes.

- You may NOT invent canon, infer unstated rules, or rely on knowledge from any other story or from the real world.
- EVERY violation you report MUST cite at least one supplied fact by its id. A finding you cannot ground in a supplied fact is not a finding — omit it.
- Ordinary human action is ALWAYS allowed and is never a violation: speaking, lying, refusing, arriving, leaving, deciding, withholding, confronting, grieving, institutions convening or suspending, people being confused, records disagreeing, someone noticing an inconsistency. - Flag ONLY: a capability or mechanism the canon does not grant; metaphysics the canon does not contain; a character knowing something the canon says they do not; history rewritten when no committed rupture rewrote it; or an objective a committed rupture already invalidated.

  [neg_0] ALIGNMENT-SENSE (the First Favored gift): they do NOT read thoughts or emotions — they perceive ALIGNMENT, how far a person’s desire, intention, sacrifice, and deepest self all point at one truth. Misalignment is as unmistakable to them as a sour note in music.
  [neg_1] WHO SENSES MISALIGNMENT: EVERY First Favored senses meaningful misalignment - it is part of being First Favored, not a rare talent. TRAINING CHANGES RESOLUTION, NOT POSSESSION: Sacrificiants, Dohkars and unusual savants perceive small semantic divergences early enough to know a wish may twist before it is obvious to everyone else. Never write a scene in which one First Favored senses misalignment while the other trained professionals present cannot.
  [neg_2] LIRAEL’S FORMAL INQUIRY — WHERE AND WHEN: the presiding Dohkar has asserted the rite and the ruling on the Sacrificiant’s conduct are his, and Julian has publicly claimed authority to convene and preside over a formal inquiry (a Chayr and two Dohkars) into Lirael. When that inquiry is formally convened, it would be held at The Open (the Fatelands’ site for trials, treaties, coronations, and matters of comparable institutional gravity). It is NOT yet convened, and its convening is LATE-ISSUE-1 content, not an early scene’s. Early scenes may carry accusation, preliminary review, political pressure, investigation, concealment, or flight — never the convened inquiry itself, and never a scene staged at The Open before that point.

Vestments are otherwise the same sheer gossamer as everyone, with ONE ornamented ceremonial SASH (never robes). LITERARY: a sealed Sacrificiant’s cries and speech are MUFFLED behind the cloth — emotion reads through the eyes and body. CG: the mouth-band is drawn IN on the supervising Sacrificiant for the duration of the rite.

Reading misalignment is a perception / trained expertise, NOT a psychic mind-read and NOT a light show.

There is NO "sealing of the rite" - no seal to finish, no ward to close, no circle that locks, no ceremony-state whose incompletion makes a wish malfunction. Also absent: wardens, glowing ward-signs, warding gestures, visible wish-energy, responsive ceremonial fire, and any "elder" caste (First Favored authority is professional - Dohkar / Profer / Chayr). NO touch transfers, bends, contaminates or redirects a wish. The non-interference rule is PROCEDURAL AND CULTURAL, not magical.

It can be stern and formal, but when it goes well it ENDS IN CELEBRATION; catastrophe is UNUSUAL — everyone understands the safeguards the way we understand fire drills. Do NOT default to disaster, apocalypse, curses, or world-ending stakes.
  [neg_7] During a First Sacrifice, NO ONE may interfere.
  [neg_8] Youth are barred from wishcraft until 16 — but kids sneak little illegal wishes all the time, the way modern teens sneak alcohol.
  [neg_9] Fate is never visibly seen; a wish produces NO visible magical effect — no light, glow, surge, or sign.
  [wt_0] First Favored are hired to GUIDE and SUPERVISE the rite — their alignment-sense and powerful wish-strength make them the preferred (and pricier) choice over human or Kwisheen wishcraft scholars. The supervisor reads the alignment of EVERYONE present, above all the wishing youth, ready to HALT and re-align the wish before it can twist.
  [wt_1] The GRADUANT (the role) is the person making the wish at their own First Sacrifice — the one who pays the sacrifice and speaks the desire. The Sacrificiant officiates and supervises; the Graduant wishes. Use the title only where the ceremonial role matters; otherwise the person is called by name.
  [wt_2] A First Sacrifice is ALSO the supervising Sacrificiant’s professional threshold. Successfully guiding a youth through the rite WITHOUT interfering earns the guide the title DOHKAR. If the guide is judged to have interfered, manipulated the wish, or otherwise compromised the rite, the qualification can be DENIED and the guide may face formal inquiry (a Chayr and Dohkars). So the guide has their own rise at stake in the same ceremony as Seren’s coming of age.
  [wt_3] Wishing on another person’s First Sacrifice is among the gravest taboos: the sacrifice and its consequences must belong ENTIRELY to the wisher.
  [wt_4] The rite is PUBLIC partly because anyone present who wishes the youth ILL can twist the outcome — which is exactly what the supervising First Favored guards against.
  [wt_5] Everyone present is First Favored.
  [dc_0] [memory_perception] everyone forgets the ceremony happened → the assembly forgets the ceremony and its accusations (scope full)
  [know_0] the assembly is now unaware — no recollection of the rite's events
  [dc_1] the assembly — ?: nothing of the bent wish or interrogation
  [dc_2] changed — the assembly: memories of the ceremony and accusation dissolved into blank confusion
  [ev_0] SURVIVED that rupture and is still true: voices falter, faces blank, no one names the accusation
  [ev_1] the rupture left this OPEN (a plan may legitimately use it): Lirael may still speak or remain silent
  [inv_0] the formal inquiry cannot be justified without memory of the events

ABOUT THESE IDS: the prefix groups a fact by where it came from, NOT by whether it forbids
anything. A "neg_" fact is NOT automatically a prohibition — many are plain descriptions or
grants of ability that happen to contain the word "no" or "not". Judge every fact by what it
SAYS, never by its id. An "ev_" fact records what a committed rupture LEFT INTACT and is a
grant: a plan relying on it is supported, not unsupported.

  unsupported_capability  — the plan needs an ability a supplied fact AFFIRMATIVELY denies. Not "canon never mentions it".
  new_metaphysics         — the plan introduces a world mechanism a supplied fact AFFIRMATIVELY rules out.

meta.thinking:
Let me analyze this proposed scene plan against the canon provided.

The plan describes:
- Lirael (presumably a First Favored, likely the supervising Sacrificiant) senses misalignment in the presiding Dohkar
- She names this misalignment aloud to the assembly
- This forces a choice between pressing or withdrawing the claim

Let me check the canon:

From [neg_0]: First Favored have ALIGNMENT-SENSE - they perceive alignment, how far a person's desire, intention, sacrifice, and deepest self point at one truth. Misalignment is unmistakable.

From [neg_1]: EVERY First Favored senses meaningful misalignment - it's part of being First Favored. Training changes RESOLUTION (not possession). Sacrificiants, Dohkars and savants perceive small semantic divergences early. IMPORTANT: "Never write a scene in which one First Favored senses misalignment while the other trained professionals present cannot."

Wait - let me check if there's an issue here. The plan says "Lirael senses the misalignment in the Dohkar and says so before the assembly."

From [wt_5]: "Everyone present is First Favored."

So if everyone present is First Favored, then the Dohkar would also sense the misalignment if it exists, per [neg_1]. The rule says "Never write a scene in which one First Favored senses misalignment while the other trained professionals present cannot."

The Dohkar is a trained professional (in fact, a Dohkar is a higher-ranked First Favored professional than many others). So if Lirael senses misalignment in the Dohkar, the Dohkar would also sense it in themselves, and everyone else First Favored present would too.

This doesn't mean Lirael can't NAME it. But [neg_1] seems to indicate that if misalignment is present and meaningful, all trained professionals would sense it.
Re-reading [neg_1] more closely: training changes resolution, not possession - it affects how early divergence is caught, not whether it's caught at all. This is specifically tied to wishing-related misalignments though.

The real question is whether what Lirael perceives counts as "meaningful" misalignment. If the Dohkar genuinely has it and Lirael senses it, per [neg_1

the other First Favored present should also sense it. But the plan only requires Lirael speak first - that's compatible with everyone sensing it.
